newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-NO LET DOWN AS ELS GRABS BUICK CLASSIC LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NO LET DOWN AS ELS GRABS BUICK CLASSIC LEAD.

text.p: Any worries about a post-U.S. Open let down were quickly dispelled by Ernie Els, who fired a seven-under-par 64 to grab the lead after the first round of the Buick Classic on Thursday.

The newly-crowned U.S. Open champion had expressed concern ahead of his defence of his Buick Classic title that he would find it difficult to focus on competition so soon after claiming a major championship.

"Starting with two birdies got my mind on golf again," said the 27-year-old South African, who claimed his second U.S. Open crown just four days ago. "I'm playing well, so I should go for it while I can."
Els, who won this tournament by a whopping eight strokes last year, held a two-shot lead over Brad Faxon.
Els carded eight birdies over his first 18 holes on the Westchester Country Club course, which is half the number he recorded in 72 holes at Congressional during the U.S. Open last week.

Faxon birdied three of the last four holes and finished five under par at 66 to seize sole possession of second place. Vijay Singh of Fiji, a two time winner here, Paul Azinger, Jim Furyk, and Jeff Maggert, one of Els's final round rivals at the Open, were tied for third another stroke back at 67.
The leaders had in common a love of the golf course -- a hilly, old-fashioned lay-out -- as well as past success at Westchester.

Els has never finished lower than fourth here, Singh has won twice in playoffs and both Azinger and Maggert have recorded runner-up finishes at Westchester. Faxon and Furyk say Westchester is their favourite course on the PGA Tour.
Maggert, who lost five strokes over the last four holes at Congressional to finish fourth last week, committed to this tournament at the last minute.
"I was playing well, I needed the Ryder Cup points, and I knew that I could do good things on this course," Maggert said.

"When I woke up Monday morning (following the Open), I don't think I've ever been more motivated to go out and make things happen. I feel the next six to eight weeks are going to be key for me. I think I can win tournaments, and I want to make the Ryder Cup team," Maggert said.

The participation of Masters champion Tiger Woods caused a stir in Westchester and, as usual, swelled the galleries. Woods also picked up where he left off at the U.S. Open, but unlike Els, for Woods than meant inconsistency and bogeys.
Woods, who finished tied for 19th last week, bogeyed four of the first six holes, a seeming extention of his Congressional woes.
But the 21-year-old sensation recovered from his rough start, and birdies on the ninth, 17th and 18th holes brought him back to one-over 72.
"The thing that's encouraging is that I'm very happy with the way I hit the ball on the last four holes. I didn't miss a shot," said Woods, who starts Friday eight shots back of Els.
"I should be able to go out and shoot a good round tomorrow," he predicted.

Woods will be playing that round without his regular caddie, Mike "Fluff" Cowan, who will be attending the funeral of Jeff "Squeeky" Medlen, Nick Price's popular former caddie, who died on Tuesday of leukaemia.
